name: Elobixibat
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Elobixibat acts in the gut and is barely absorbed: about 0.01% of a dose appears in urine and protein binding exceeds 99% [[PI]]. The Philippine insert gives no kidney-based dose adjustment [[PI]]. Small studies in CKD stages G3 to G5 and on hemodialysis used the usual 5 to 15 mg/day and found better bowel function without serious adverse events [[JENAKSORNKUL2024,SHONO2024,MATSUYAMA2022,KAMEI2020]]. "No adjustment specified" is not the same as proven safety at every level of kidney function: there are no dedicated kidney-impairment pharmacokinetic studies, and data for peritoneal dialysis, CRRT and acute kidney injury are lacking.
kidney_function_basis: The insert sets no kidney function threshold; bands are shown on eGFR for orientation only.

bands.recommendation: 10 mg once daily before a meal; adjust to symptoms; maximum 15 mg/day (PH insert).

No kidney-based adjustment in the PH insert; about 0.01% of a dose is excreted in urine. A small retrospective study included CKD G3 (Matsuyama 2022). Usual dose; watch for diarrhea and volume depletion.
No kidney-based adjustment in the PH insert. A small retrospective study included CKD G4 (Matsuyama 2022). Usual dose; watch for diarrhea and volume depletion.

No kidney-based adjustment in the PH insert. Data are limited (9 non-dialysis G5 patients in one study, Matsuyama 2022). In a large Japanese database, stage 5 CKD was associated with stopping elobixibat (Masaki 2023).

hd.text: No adjustment specified in the PH insert. Studied at 10 mg/day in a 12-week randomized trial (taken at bedtime in that trial; Jenaksornkul 2024) and at 5 to 15 mg/day long term (Shono 2024). No supplemental dose is described. Diarrhea can affect volume status and electrolytes.

pd.text: Not specifically studied (3 peritoneal dialysis patients in one mixed cohort, Matsuyama 2022). The PH insert gives no adjustment; urinary excretion is minimal.

dialyzable: Not studied; plasma levels are very low and protein binding exceeds 99% (PH insert).
monitoring: Bowel frequency, abdominal pain and diarrhea; if diarrhea develops, volume status, blood pressure and electrolytes (clinical interpretation).
